answer: Picture a registry where each grading seat must post a stake that the protocol burns, never refunds, once that seat is proven to be a second identity of the same operator. Splitting one budget across many accounts now multiplies a sunk loss per seat, so the attacker is pushed off the ledge of cheap duplication to an island of real expense, and a single honest operator keeps one seat without penalty. Correlation over shared funding reveals the cluster too, so every extra vote costs fresh money and the falcon of a mass attack loses its speed and its profit.
